business_problem: Betclic needed to replace a centralized SQL monolith that delayed live betting updates, created platform-wide failure risks, and slowed search and back-office feature delivery.
solution_summary: Betclic replaced a centralized on-premises SQL monolith with MongoDB Atlas so it could deliver live betting data fast enough for in-play wagering while giving domain teams more ownership over infrastructure. Instead of pointing every microservice at one primary database, Betclic assigns dedicated MongoDB clusters to business subdomains and isolates logical databases so teams can move independently. The company automates scaling with Terraform and AWS Lambda, increasing cluster capacity before matches and scaling down afterward on a defined schedule. MongoDB Search on Atlas provides integrated search indexes for back-office and customer-facing queries, and developers can use the $search operator inside normal MongoDB pipelines rather than synchronizing a separate search engine. By tuning connection handling and bulk-write patterns, Betclic turned MongoDB Atlas into the low-latency operational core for odds distribution, search, and high-volume traffic spikes across its betting platform.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores live betting data for Betclic’s domain-oriented subplatforms and provides the managed low-latency database backbone.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Search on Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs integrated search indexes for customer-facing and back-office queries without a separate search engine.

data_flow: Event and odds data are written into domain-specific MongoDB Atlas clusters, searched through Atlas Search indexes, and served to betting, back-office, and customer-facing services that need low-latency updates during live matches.
business_outcome: Betclic reduced live-data latency, improved reliability, removed team bottlenecks, and built a platform that can keep scaling into new countries and higher betting volumes.
metrics: The legacy platform introduced up to 10 seconds of end-to-end latency on live betting data.
Betclic cut end-to-end latency to around 400 milliseconds and kept standard read latency under 5 milliseconds.
The new platform handles nearly 100,000 reads per second and 50,000 writes per second without major database incidents.
architecture_clues: Betclic assigns dedicated MongoDB clusters to business subdomains instead of using one central database.
Terraform and AWS Lambda scale clusters up before matches and down afterward.
MongoDB Search on Atlas keeps search indexes synchronized inside the main database platform.
Developers tuned drivers to keep idle connections live during sudden traffic spikes.
